passage:
After a small earthquake, Jay's family prepared emergency bags. Each bag had water, food, a flashlight, medicine, copies of important documents, and a whistle.
Jay thought it was unnecessary because the earthquake had not caused serious damage. His mother said preparation is easiest before fear arrives.
At school, Jay's teacher asked students to discuss emergency plans. Jay realized many classmates did not know where their families would meet if phones failed.
That night, he helped his younger brother pack a small bag too.
Emergency preparation is not a sign that people expect disaster every day. It is a quiet promise to act more calmly if one comes.
